`friendlycells` computes similarity between spatial transcriptomics samples based on which labels (e.g. cell types) border one another. It is available for R and Python and is compatible with Visium, Visium HD (binned or segmented) and Xenium. ## Installation ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ```r remotes::install_github("george-hall-ucl/friendlycells", subdir = "R") ``` Requires `dbscan` and `deldir`. ## Python ```bash pip install "git+https://github.com/george-hall-ucl/friendlycells#subdirectory=python" ``` Requires `pandas`, `numpy` and `scipy`. ::: ## Quick start The main function is `spatial_similarity()`, which receives a [named list]{.lang-r}[dict]{.lang-py} of [data frames]{.lang-r}[DataFrames]{.lang-py}, one for each sample in the comparison. Each sample's [data frame]{.lang-r}[DataFrame]{.lang-py} comprises three columns: * `x` (horizontal coordinates, e.g. in pixels or micrometres) * `y` (vertical coordinates, e.g. in pixels or micrometres) * `label` (what you want to test for connections between, e.g. cell types). Select your language and technology to see how to make this [list]{.lang-r}[dict]{.lang-py} and run `spatial_similarity()`. ```{=html}

``` ::: {.snippet .lang-r .tech-visium} ```r library(Seurat) library(friendlycells) # Assume you have two Visium samples, `healthy` and `diseased`, loaded using # Seurat and you want to compare them using the annotated `cell_type` metadata. samples <- list() samples[["healthy"]] <- data.frame(x = GetTissueCoordinates(healthy)$x, y = GetTissueCoordinates(healthy)$y, label = healthy$cell_type) samples[["diseased"]] <- data.frame(x = GetTissueCoordinates(diseased)$x, y = GetTissueCoordinates(diseased)$y, label = diseased$cell_type) sim <- spatial_similarity(samples) ``` ::: ::: {.snippet .lang-py .tech-visium} ```python import pandas as pd from friendlycells import spatial_similarity # Assume you have two Visium samples, `healthy` and `diseased`, loaded as # AnnData objects (e.g. using squidpy's `sq.read.visium()`), and you want to # compare them using the annotated `cell_type` column of `.obs`. samples = {} samples["healthy"] = pd.DataFrame({ "x": healthy.obsm["spatial"][:, 0], "y": healthy.obsm["spatial"][:, 1], "label": healthy.obs["cell_type"], }) samples["diseased"] = pd.DataFrame({ "x": diseased.obsm["spatial"][:, 0], "y": diseased.obsm["spatial"][:, 1], "label": diseased.obs["cell_type"], }) sim = spatial_similarity(samples) ``` ::: ::: {.snippet .lang-r .tech-hd-bins} ```r library(Seurat) library(friendlycells) # Assume you have two Visium HD samples, `healthy` and `diseased`, loaded using # Seurat at a single bin size (e.g. `Load10X_Spatial(dir, bin.size = 8)`), and # you want to compare them using the annotated `cell_type` metadata. samples <- list() samples[["healthy"]] <- data.frame(x = GetTissueCoordinates(healthy)$x, y = GetTissueCoordinates(healthy)$y, label = healthy$cell_type) samples[["diseased"]] <- data.frame(x = GetTissueCoordinates(diseased)$x, y = GetTissueCoordinates(diseased)$y, label = diseased$cell_type) sim <- spatial_similarity(samples) ``` ::: ::: {.snippet .lang-py .tech-hd-bins} ```python import pandas as pd from friendlycells import spatial_similarity # Assume you have two Visium HD samples, `healthy` and `diseased`, loaded as # AnnData tables of a single bin size (e.g. `sdata.tables["square_008um"]`, # using spatialdata-io's `visium_hd()`), and you want to compare them using # the annotated `cell_type` column of `.obs`. samples = {} samples["healthy"] = pd.DataFrame({ "x": healthy.obsm["spatial"][:, 0], "y": healthy.obsm["spatial"][:, 1], "label": healthy.obs["cell_type"], }) samples["diseased"] = pd.DataFrame({ "x": diseased.obsm["spatial"][:, 0], "y": diseased.obsm["spatial"][:, 1], "label": diseased.obs["cell_type"], }) sim = spatial_similarity(samples) ``` ::: ::: {.snippet .lang-r .tech-hd-cells} ```r library(Seurat) library(friendlycells) # Assume you have two Visium HD samples, `healthy` and `diseased`, loaded using # Seurat with segmented cells (`Load10X_Spatial(dir, bin.size = "polygons")`), # and you want to compare them using the annotated `cell_type` metadata. samples <- list() samples[["healthy"]] <- data.frame(x = GetTissueCoordinates(healthy)$x, y = GetTissueCoordinates(healthy)$y, label = healthy$cell_type) samples[["diseased"]] <- data.frame(x = GetTissueCoordinates(diseased)$x, y = GetTissueCoordinates(diseased)$y, label = diseased$cell_type) sim <- spatial_similarity(samples) ``` ::: ::: {.snippet .lang-py .tech-hd-cells} ```python import pandas as pd from friendlycells import spatial_similarity # Assume you have two Visium HD samples, `healthy` and `diseased`, loaded as # SpatialData objects using spatialdata-io's `visium_hd()`, and you want to # compare them using the annotated `cell_type` column of the cell segmentation # table. Each cell's position is the centroid of its outline. samples = {} table = healthy.tables["cell_segmentations"] cells = healthy.shapes[table.obs["region"].iloc[0]].centroid.loc[table.obs_names] samples["healthy"] = pd.DataFrame({ "x": cells.x, "y": cells.y, "label": table.obs["cell_type"], }) table = diseased.tables["cell_segmentations"] cells = diseased.shapes[table.obs["region"].iloc[0]].centroid.loc[table.obs_names] samples["diseased"] = pd.DataFrame({ "x": cells.x, "y": cells.y, "label": table.obs["cell_type"], }) sim = spatial_similarity(samples) ``` ::: ::: {.snippet .lang-r .tech-xenium} ```r library(Seurat) library(friendlycells) # Assume you have two Xenium samples, `healthy` and `diseased`, loaded using # Seurat (`LoadXenium()`), and you want to compare them using the annotated # `cell_type` metadata. samples <- list() samples[["healthy"]] <- data.frame(x = GetTissueCoordinates(healthy)$x, y = GetTissueCoordinates(healthy)$y, label = healthy$cell_type) samples[["diseased"]] <- data.frame(x = GetTissueCoordinates(diseased)$x, y = GetTissueCoordinates(diseased)$y, label = diseased$cell_type) sim <- spatial_similarity(samples) ``` ::: ::: {.snippet .lang-py .tech-xenium} ```python import pandas as pd from friendlycells import spatial_similarity # Assume you have two Xenium samples, `healthy` and `diseased`, loaded as # AnnData tables (e.g. `sdata.tables["table"]`, using spatialdata-io's # `xenium()`), and you want to compare them using the annotated `cell_type` # column of `.obs`. samples = {} samples["healthy"] = pd.DataFrame({ "x": healthy.obsm["spatial"][:, 0], "y": healthy.obsm["spatial"][:, 1], "label": healthy.obs["cell_type"], }) samples["diseased"] = pd.DataFrame({ "x": diseased.obsm["spatial"][:, 0], "y": diseased.obsm["spatial"][:, 1], "label": diseased.obs["cell_type"], }) sim = spatial_similarity(samples) ``` ::: This returns a sample × sample matrix of similarity scores: 1 = identical, 0 = least similar pair. See the [vignette](vignette.qmd) for a worked example, and [Reference](reference.qmd) for full documentation of all options. As inter-sample similarities are calculated in terms of neighboring `label`s, different definitions of "neighborhoods" will lead to different results. By default, `friendlycells` tries to use a sensible definition for each technology. You can check that your neighborhoods are sensible for your data by visualizing them using `plot_neighborhoods()`. More information about different neighborhood definitions can be found [here](neighborhoods.qmd). ## Citation The original algorithm and implementation of `friendlycells` were first published in: - Durkin _et al_. "Functional integration of an autologous engineered esophagus in a large-animal model." _Nature Biotechnology_ (2026). - Budinger _et al_. "An in vivo and in vitro spatiotemporal profile of human midbrain development." _Nature Communications_ (2026).
